description: On a runner with Docker and systemd: report mode changes nothing and shows the expected-containers list it would create; apply creates the list once, from every container present, marks it not reviewed, and never rewrites it, and installs an enabled prune timer whose script never touches volumes. The prune refuses an age limit under 24 hours, so the tests make their containers and images 30 days old rather than lower it (a container by stopping Docker and editing config.v2.json; an image by loading a docker save archive written by hand, with the date in it). Before the list is reviewed, the prune removes no container and no image. After review, a stopped container that nothing protects is first recorded in /var/lib/tc-docker/pending-removal (0700 root directory, 0600 file) and left alone; a run inside the grace period leaves it and says until when; a run after it (the record moved back 145 hours) removes it and drops the record. Its age counts from when it stopped: one stopped 29 days ago and one never started, created 30 days ago, are recorded; one created 30 days ago that stopped just now is not (the times are set by stopping Docker and editing config.v2.json). A recorded container added to the list, or started again, loses its record. When the record cannot be written (a read-only bind mount), no container is removed and the exit is 1, through the timer's script and through Prune now; a GRACE_HOURS under 24 written by hand is refused by the prune; an OLDER_THAN_HOURS that is 0, 23, 8761, empty, not a number, quoted or followed by anything is refused too, with nothing at all recorded or removed and exit 1, while 8760 and 24 are used; the settings file is read as text and never run (commands on other lines, a command substitution or an arithmetic subscript as a value: nothing runs, and such a value is refused, except in a PRUNE_IMAGES line, which is only named as no longer used), and the last line for a name wins; and when the review is withdrawn the prune removes nothing and clears the record. Stopped containers that are on the list, have an unless-stopped policy, or are labelled tc.keep are kept with their images. Images: the untagged image built 30 days ago is removed and named, one made just now is kept, and the tagged ones (one labelled tc.keep) are kept, and a docker shim that records the prune's docker commands shows none that could reach a registry; a failing docker image ls removes no image and exits 1. The last steps restart Docker on the other image store and check the same there, so both stores are covered whichever the runner starts with. Bad input is refused with exit 2 before anything is written. A host without Docker is Tier 2. A container label is untrusted: one whose Compose project label carries a forged row cannot add a row or a field to the container listing, so a reviewed prune keeps the listed stopped container the forged row named, names the containers whose labels cannot be read, keeps them, and never prints the label; a new list leaves them off and says so. When docker ps fails but docker info answers (a shim on PATH), the prune prints ERROR, exits 1 and removes nothing, and does not reach its network or build-cache step; Prune now exits 1; and the list is not created, exit 3. Docker stopped (docker.service stopped, docker.socket still listening, a restart: always container on the list): the prune service has Requisite=docker.service and After=, not Requires=; starting it, by hand or when the timer itself fires, does not start Docker and does not run the prune, and the timer stays active; the prune run by hand prints one line saying Docker is not running, removes nothing and exits 0; the component in Report and in Apply (exit 0: neither needs Docker), in Apply with Prune now (which does not run, exit 3), and with no list (not created, exit 3) leaves docker.service inactive; started again, the timer's service runs the prune normally. A changed service file or prune script is rewritten with a daemon-reload and the timer is not restarted (same ActiveEnterTimestamp and NextElapseUSecRealtime, no prune run); a schedule change restarts it. With no docker.service unit (its file, drop-ins and /etc/init.d/docker moved away), the service is written without the dependency lines and says so, and the unit starts and runs the prune; with the unit back, the next run writes them again. Version 13: the installed prune reads the pending-removal file with the shared tc_pending_lines and has no parser of its own; and a pending-removal file with a comment, a blank line, a malformed line, a CRLF line and a second line for the same container gives what version 12 gave: two unreadable lines counted and dropped, the first line for the container used, nothing removed early, and the file written again clean. Version 14: the installed prune writes pending-removal with tc_state_write, the function in the block marked tc-docker state that the three Docker monitors share (a step reads the installed prune for it). A /var/lib/tc-docker that is not owned by root is not used and not taken over, and a symlink in the record's place is not followed, written through or replaced: either way no container is removed and the prune exits 1; with the record a regular file again, the same prune removes the container whose record is due. The script's opening comment is short and points to the README (a step reads it). Version 15: the daemon.json part is in Docker - Configure Daemon Limits [Lin], with its tests. Here, a step reads the script for what is left of it (nothing: no python3, none of the four input variables); Apply, a job that still passes those four variables (with values version 14 refused), and every other run in this spec leave daemon.json as it was, with no backup and no staging file beside it. Version 16: there is no All mode. A step reads the script for what is left of it (nothing: no usrPruneImages, no PRUNE_IMAGES written, no registry lookup code); the settings file has no PRUNE_IMAGES line; one left in it (all, dangling, ALL, a value version 15 refused, a command substitution) is not an error: the prune names it once, runs nothing from it, keeps every tagged image and exits 0, on both image stores; a job that still passes usrPruneImages (All, or a value version 15 refused with exit 2) runs as a normal one, and the settings file is written again without the line.

cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-age <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-age NAME=CREATED[,FINISHED] ...: stop Docker, set those containers' Created
# (and State.FinishedAt) in their config.v2.json, start Docker again. Docker sets both
# times itself and has no way to change them, so this is how a test makes a container old.
set -e
declare -A ids
for a in "$@"; do ids[${a%%=*}]=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "${a%%=*}"); done
root=$(docker info --format '{{.DockerRootDir}}')
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then systemctl stop docker.socket docker.service; else pkill -x dockerd; while pgrep -x dockerd >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done; fi
for a in "$@"; do
  n=${a%%=*}; v=${a#*=}; c=${v%%,*}; f="$root/containers/${ids[$n]}/config.v2.json"
  if [ "$v" != "$c" ]; then jq --arg c "$c" --arg f "${v#*,}" '.Created=$c | .State.FinishedAt=$f' "$f" > "$f.tc"
  else jq --arg c "$c" '.Created=$c' "$f" > "$f.tc"; fi
  mv "$f.tc" "$f"
done
if [ -d /run/systemd/system ]; then systemctl start docker.service; else (setsid dockerd >/var/log/tc-test-dockerd.log 2>&1 </dev/null &); fi
for i in $(seq 30); do docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && break; sleep 1; done
for a in "$@"; do docker inspect -f '{{.Name}} created {{.Created}}, finished {{.State.FinishedAt}}' "${a%%=*}"; done
EOF

cat > /usr/local/sbin/tc-test-old-image <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# tc-test-old-image LABEL [TAG]: load an image, built here, whose build time (Created) is
# 30 days ago; labelled LABEL (key=value) and tc.nonce; tagged TAG, or untagged. Prints
# its id. docker import and docker build stamp an image with the time now, and the prune
# never removes an image younger than OLDER_THAN_HOURS (24 at the least), so this is how
# a test makes an old one: a docker save archive written by hand, with the date in it.
set -e
label=$1; tag=${2:-}
w=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$w"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$w/root/bin"; cp /bin/true "$w/root/bin/"
tar -C "$w/root" -cf "$w/layer.tar" .
c=$(date -u -d '30 days ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
jq -cn --arg c "$c" --arg a "$(docker version --format '{{.Server.Arch}}')" --arg d "sha256:$(sha256sum "$w/layer.tar" | cut -d' ' -f1)" --arg n "$(date +%s%N)" --arg k "${label%%=*}" --arg v "${label#*=}" '{architecture:$a,os:"linux",created:$c,config:{Labels:{"tc.nonce":$n,($k):$v}},rootfs:{type:"layers",diff_ids:[$d]},history:[{created:$c,created_by:"tc-test"}]}' > "$w/config.json"
cfg=$(sha256sum "$w/config.json" | cut -d' ' -f1); mv "$w/config.json" "$w/$cfg.json"
jq -cn --arg cfg "$cfg.json" --arg t "$tag" '[{Config:$cfg,RepoTags:(if $t == "" then null else [$t] end),Layers:["layer.tar"]}]' > "$w/manifest.json"
tar -C "$w" -cf "$w/image.tar" manifest.json "$cfg.json" layer.tar
out=$(docker load -i "$w/image.tar")
if [ -n "$tag" ]; then docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "$tag"; else printf '%s\n' "$out" | sed -n 's/^Loaded image ID: //p' | grep .; fi
EOF

store)

aside)

        printf '%s\n' "$used" | grep -qx "$id" && continue

images)

has)
    shift
    for n in "$@"; do docker image inspect "$n" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "$n kept" || echo "$n GONE"; done ;;
esac
